# Relationship to Existing Skill Systems

How MCP Skills Extension compares to current skill/instruction systems.

## Agent Skills Specification (agentskills.io)

The Agent Skills spec is the **format standard** that SEP-2640 builds on [3][12].
Open standard since December 18, 2025 [15]. Adopted by 26+ platforms including
Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, VS Code,
and ChatGPT [15].

**Key stats** (February 2026 study) [15]:
- 40,285 published skills
- 18.5x growth in 20 days (January 16 to February 5)
- Median skill size: 1,414 tokens
- Web search/retrieval skills averaged 1,268 installs

The relationship: Agent Skills defines the *format* (SKILL.md + frontmatter);
SEP-2640 defines the *transport* (how to serve and discover skills over MCP) [3].
SEP-2640 "explicitly delegates format details to agentskills.io rather than
redefining them in MCP" [3].

Microsoft adopted the Agent Skills spec for their Agent Framework [18].

## Claude Code Skills (Local Files)

Claude Code loads skills from local directories — typically
`~/.claude/skills/` or plugin skill directories. Skills are SKILL.md files
with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`, and implementation-specific
fields like `model`, `hooks`, `agent`).

**Non-standard fields already shipped** by Claude Code and other
implementations [11]:
- `disable-model-invocation`
- `user-invocable`
- `model`
- `context`
- `agent`
- `hooks`
- `argument-hint`

These fields are outside the Agent Skills spec's 6 allowed fields [11][12].
SEP-2640 does not standardize them — they remain implementation-specific.

## Comparison: Local Skills vs MCP Skills

| Aspect | Local Skills | MCP Skills (SEP-2640) |
|--------|-------------|----------------------|
| Discovery | Filesystem scan at startup | skill:// resources + optional index.json [3] |
| Distribution | Copy files / git clone / npx skills add | MCP resource serving from connected servers [3] |
| Updates | Manual (git pull, reinstall) | Dynamic via resource subscriptions [4] |
| Multi-server | N/A (local only) | Cross-server composition supported [4][6] |
| Execution | Hooks, scripts, commands run locally | Untrusted input — no implicit execution [3] |
| Format | SKILL.md + non-standard extensions | SKILL.md (Agent Skills spec only) [3][12] |
| Availability | Persistent on disk | Ephemeral — no permanent footprint [4] |

## Working Group Implementations

| Implementation | Approach | Differentiator |
|----------------|----------|----------------|
| skilljack-mcp | Tools + prompts + file watching | Audience annotations [8] |

## AGENTS.md / .cursorrules / CLAUDE.md

These are **project-level instruction files** — not skills. AGENTS.md
reduced runtime by 28.6% and token usage by 16.6% across 124 PRs in one
study [17]. Skills differ from these files in three ways:

1. **Contextual activation** — skills load only when task requires them;
   instruction files load every session [12][15]
2. **Portability** — SKILL.md works across 26+ platforms; CLAUDE.md is
   Claude Code-specific, .cursorrules is Cursor-specific [15]
3. **Progressive disclosure** — skills support multi-file structures with
   on-demand resource loading [12]

## Gaps and Limitations

- 26+ platform adoption claim [15] is from a single blog source and may
  count platforms with minimal or experimental support
- Non-standard frontmatter fields (hooks, agent, model) create a
  compatibility gap between what Claude Code uses and what the Agent Skills
  spec allows [11][12]
- MCP Skills Extension adds transport, not format — the format
  compatibility with local skills depends on which frontmatter fields the
  skill uses
